content: Take your medication exactly as prescribed. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to determine the appropriate course of action. Storage Instructions: Follow the storage guidelines provided in the product instructions or by your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Famotidine is used to treat ulcers in the stomach and intestines and to prevent the recurrence of intestinal ulcers after they have healed. It is also used to manage certain stomach and esophagus conditions, such as erosive esophagitis, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Famotidine works by reducing the amount of acid produced by the stomach, alleviating symptoms such as persistent cough, stomach pain, heartburn, and difficulty swallowing. This form of famotidine is administered intravenously and is intended for short-term use when oral administration is not possible. How to Use: This medication is injected into a vein as directed by your doctor. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on preparation and usage. Before injecting each dose, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Inspect the product visually for particles or discoloration before use. Do not use the liquid if either is present. Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, constipation, diarrhea, or pain/redness at the injection site. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions are rare but seek immediate medical attention if they occur. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using famotidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other H2 blockers (e.g., cimetidine, ranitidine), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. During pregnancy, famotidine should only be used when clearly necessary. This drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some products require stomach acid for proper absorption, and famotidine may affect their efficacy by reducing stomach acid. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lifestyle Changes: To enhance the effectiveness of this medication, consider lifestyle modifications such as stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol intake, and dietary changes (e.g., avoiding caffeine and certain spices). Monitoring: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., endoscopy, kidney function) may be conducted while you are using this medication. Attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
